introduction.p: Fluid pressure increases with depth. To compute the force on a submerged surface, divide it into strips narrow enough that the pressure is nearly constant on each strip. Multiply the pressure by the strip area and integrate.

subsection.title: Force on a vertical plate
subsection.p: A vertical plate in water feels different pressure at different depths. Horizontal strips solve the problem because each thin horizontal strip has nearly one depth.

exercise.title: Why do hydrostatic-force problems use horizontal strips?

statement.p: A vertical plate feels different pressure at different depths. In your own words, why does a thin horizontal strip have nearly one depth, and why would a vertical strip mix many pressures in one piece?

hint.p: Choose a small piece on which the quantity that varies is almost constant. Here that quantity is depth, so the strip should follow a level line.

subsection.title: Choosing strips
subsection.p: Hydrostatic pressure depends on depth. So horizontal strips are natural.
A vertical strip would contain many depths at once, and the pressure would vary along the strip. A horizontal strip stays at one depth, up to a tiny error that disappears in the limit.

p.me: \text{For hydrostatic force on a vertical plate, use horizontal strips.}

warning.title: Warning
warning.p: Hydrostatic force is not determined by area alone. Depth matters.
Two plates with the same area can feel different total forces if one has more of its area deeper in the water.

exercise.title: Why can two plates with the same area feel different forces?

statement.p: Turning a triangular plate upside down keeps the area the same but can double the force. In your own words, why is hydrostatic force not determined by area alone, and what does it mean to put more area deeper?

hint.p: Deeper water pushes harder. A plate with more of its area at large depth accumulates more force, even if the total area has not changed.

subsection.title: Dams and windows
subsection.p: Dams and underwater windows are the most common places where hydrostatic force matters.
A dam is wide, and the water depth changes from top to bottom. A window may be small, but the pressure can still be large if it is deep.

exercise.title: Why is pressure not the same as total force?

statement.p: Pressure is force per unit area. In your own words, why may you multiply pressure by area only when the pressure is constant over that area, and why does a vertical wall force you to integrate?

hint.p: On a vertical plate, deeper strips feel more pressure than shallow ones. One pressure times the whole area would pretend the depth never changes.
